% Typed shift stepsize (TSS): a statistical procedure, not a dashboard.
% Estimators, signed LR map, and the scheduler comparison.
% Requires amsmath, booktabs. Table~\ref{tab:tss-vs-schedulers} is auto-generated.

\paragraph{Typed shift stepsize.}
Let $W$ index consecutive batches and let $X=(X^{(v)},X^{(a)},X^{(t)})$ be the concatenated video/audio/text block.
Covariate shift on modality $m$ is a change in $P(X^{(m)}\mid W)$.
Concept drift on modality $m$ is a change in $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$.
These are different identified objects and they must not share a learning-rate sign.

\emph{Covariate intensity.}
Let $z_i^{(m)}$ be the coordinate-mean of block $m$ on window $i$.
The two-sample Cohen statistic
\begin{equation}
  \hat c_m
  =
  \bigl|\,d\bigl(z^{(m)}\mid W=t-1,\; z^{(m)}\mid W=t\bigr)\bigr|
\end{equation}
is an absolute intensity, not a simplex share.
The share $\pi_m=\hat c_m/\sum_{m'}\hat c_{m'}$ remains a \emph{which-head} budget (open vision, then audio, not clip-level text).
Using $\eta_m=\eta_0\pi_m$ has the wrong sign whenever the map $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$ is still valid.

\emph{Concept intensity.}
Let $h_{t-1}^{(m)}$ be the frozen unimodal head from the previous round.
Translate the new block to the old mean, $\tilde X_t^{(m)}=X_t^{(m)}-(\bar x_t^{(m)}-\bar x_{t-1}^{(m)})$.
A pure location shift in $P(X^{(m)})$ is removed by that alignment; a change in $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$ is not.
\begin{equation}
  \hat\delta_m
  =
  \bigl(
    L(h_{t-1}^{(m)}(\tilde X_t^{(m)}),Y_t)
    -
    L(h_{t-1}^{(m)}(X_{t-1}^{(m)}),Y_{t-1})
  \bigr)_+.
\end{equation}

\emph{Signed stepsize.}
With a quiet freeze when both channels are off,
\begin{equation}
  \eta_m
  =
  \eta_0\,
  \frac{\hat\delta_m}{\hat\delta_m+\kappa}\,
  \frac{1}{1+\lambda\hat c_m},
  \qquad
  \eta_m=0
  \text{ if }
  \hat c_m<\tau_c
  \text{ and }
  \hat\delta_m<\tau_\delta.
\end{equation}
Large $\hat c_m$ lowers the step (do not chase $X$).
Large $\hat\delta_m$ raises the step (relearn the map).
Clip-level text on the MSR-VTT extract is both-quiet, so $\eta_t=0$; inverting $\pi$ would give it the largest step.

Refresh / KV invalidation is a different control: it may still follow $\hat c_m$.
TSS is the SGD map, not a memory schedule, and not a cosine lag board.

\emph{Comparators.}
Constant, step decay, cosine annealing, inverse-time, and a plateau rule (halve $\eta$ after two non-improving rounds) are scalar schedulers of $t$ or of the loss.
They cannot type the shift.
$\eta\propto\pi$ uses the same $\hat c_m$ with the opposite sign.
Oracle TSS substitutes the known $(c_m,\delta_m)$ of the simulation DGP.
Table~\ref{tab:tss-vs-schedulers} reports the Monte Carlo comparison.
On covariate-only streams the target is backward transfer (accuracy on batch~0 after the stream); on concept-only streams it is post-change accuracy.
A second labelled extract is required before claiming a downstream-task magnitude; the present MSR-VTT windows illustrate $\hat c$ and the quiet text freeze, not a finished applied study.
